result.summary: After Eira falls, the Arcadians welcome the Messenian refugees on Mount Lycæus, and Aristomenes plans a raid on Sparta. Aristocrates, a Lacedæmonian-bribed traitor, betrays the plan, is exposed by an intercepted letter, and is stoned to death by the Arcadians.

scenes.title: Arcadians Receive the Refugees
scenes.summary: The Arcadians ask Aristocrates to lead them to help the Messenians, but he refuses. Once they learn of survivors, they meet them at Mount Lycæus and offer them homes and land.
scenes.stakes: The Messenian survivors risk destitution and destruction; Arcadian aid depends on a leader who has been bribed.

scenes.title: Aristomenes' Plan Against Sparta
scenes.summary: Aristomenes picks 500 reckless Messenians and proposes a night raid on Sparta. About 300 Arcadians volunteer, but the omens delay them.
scenes.stakes: Aristomenes and his men risk death in a desperate raid, and the plan could be betrayed.

scenes.title: Aristocrates Exposed and Stoned
scenes.summary: The Arcadians intercept Aristocrates' slave carrying Anaxander's reply and learn of the betrayal. They stone Aristocrates, cast him out unburied and set up a pillar in the temple of Lycæan Zeus.
scenes.stakes: Aristocrates faces death for treason; Arcadia must deal with a perjured king.

characters.name: Aristocrates
characters.description: Arcadian king and leader, bribed by the Lacedæmonians and a twice-proved traitor

characters.name: Aristomenes
characters.description: Messenian leader who plans a raid on Sparta

characters.name: Zeus

characters.name: Arcadians

alias_notes.explanation: Zeus worshipped at his temple on Mount Lycæus in Arcadia.

notable_quotes.reason: Aristomenes' bold gamble: capture Sparta or die in deeds posterity will remember.
Aristomenes' silent grief when the Messenians look to him over Aristocrates' fate.

analysis.text: Betrayal and divine justice: Aristocrates' repeated treachery is finally exposed and punished, with Zeus invoked as guardian of oaths.
The episode comes from the Second Messenian War, and shows Arcadian ties to Messenia and the Spartan use of bribery against enemy leaders.

fun_facts.text: Pausanias records the pillar's inscription, a type of local evidence he often cites for his accounts.

language_notes.text: Eira was the Messenians' last mountain stronghold, held for years against Sparta; its fall ended the Second Messenian War.
"Raiment" means clothing; "influential persons" are men of standing sent as an honourable escort.
"Prodigal of their lives" means recklessly willing to risk death.
"For the second time" refers to his earlier desertion at the Great Trench, now repeated by this betrayal.
The Great Trench was a battle where Aristocrates, the Arcadian king allied to Messenia, treacherously withdrew his troops, causing the Messenian defeat.
Casting a body out unburied was a severe punishment, denying the dead proper rites.

context_notes.text: Anaxander was king of Sparta at this time, according to Pausanias, and Aristocrates' secret paymaster.
Lycæan Zeus was worshipped on Mount Lycæus in Arcadia, the region's chief sanctuary; a pillar there made the shame public and lasting.

literary_notes.text: The reader knows Aristocrates is a traitor while Aristomenes speaks his secret plan in front of him, making disaster feel certain.
Aristomenes' silent weeping shows his grief and restraint, contrasting the crowd's anger and hinting at his earlier trust in Aristocrates.
Time is made an agent that brings justice and uncovers the traitor, with Zeus as its partner.
